examples.name: Default
examples.summary: The panel a page closes with: one headline, one supporting sentence, and the two controls the reader is meant to choose between. The primary action leads and the secondary one is `outlined`, so the panel has a single obvious target. From `md` up the controls sit beside the copy; below it they stack and stretch full width.

examples.name: WithEyebrow
examples.summary: The same panel with an `eyebrow` above the headline. The overline names the panel when it sits mid-page and the headline alone would not say what it belongs to. It adds a line to the copy stack, so the panel grows taller while the actions stay on the headline row from `md` up.

examples.name: Types
examples.summary: The three registers. `panel` keeps the copy and both controls on one surface and reads as a row from `md` up. `split` divides the band at 7fr/3fr: the raised lead cell carries the two-tone headline and the primary action, the aside carries the supporting line and the secondary one, and each cell pushes its control to the band floor so the two share a baseline whatever the copy does. `lead` is that lead cell with no aside — the supporting line moves under the headline and every control sits in one row on the floor, which is the register for a close whose actions are peers.

examples.name: Primary
examples.summary: The loud close. The band keeps the canvas ground and owns the light: it moves the resting pools of the composed pixelate out of frame and runs its two waves at triple gain and double pace, so bright and dark bands of the primary colour keep travelling across the headline instead of a still glow. What is drawn is composed in: a pixelated `TextureMaterial` through `background`, and a benefits `Ticker` through `bottom`. The waves stand still under reduced motion.
